mechanisms.summary: KHI initiates stripping; growing RTI later pierces the droplet, while the post-detonation adverse pressure gradient weakens bulk acceleration.

evidence_candidates.claim: Detonation-driven RP-3 and water breakup proceeds from a KHI-dominated stripping stage to coupled KHI-RTI piercing and catastrophic breakup.
evidence_candidates.evidence_summary: High-speed sequences resolve early shear stripping and later RT piercing for both liquids.
evidence_candidates.limitations: Shadowgraph is a two-dimensional projection and the smallest early structures are below resolution.

evidence_candidates.claim: Shock-derived deformation and drag correlations are not directly transferable to detonation loading because the post-detonation adverse pressure gradient reduces convection and aerodynamic forcing.
evidence_candidates.evidence_summary: Detonation data collapse to dc/d0=1+0.72821t* and Cd=0.23, far below the cited shock-induced slopes/drag.
evidence_candidates.limitations: Cross-study shock comparison is secondary; primary detonation correlations are measured in this facility.

evidence_candidates.claim: Collapsed detonation breakup time differs by liquid: t*b=10.06 for water and 7.90 for RP-3, with surface tension implicated in the difference.
evidence_candidates.evidence_summary: Both case families fall within the fitted prediction bands and adapted mass-stripping equations use the two constants.
evidence_candidates.limitations: The time normalization itself excludes surface tension; the mechanism is an author interpretation supported by the liquid comparison.
